**3. Matters Arising from the Previous Minutes**
- **Action 11-24-03 (SW):** Draft revised safeguarding policy. SW reported that the policy was circulated to PN for review on 2 December. PN confirmed she would return comments by 18 December. Action remains open, deadline extended to 20 December 2024.
- **Action 11-24-07 (DO):** Obtain three quotes for replacing the clubhouse boiler. DO confirmed quotes were received from two suppliers; the third quote is still outstanding. He will chase the third supplier before the end of the week.
- **Action 11-24-09 (TR):** Organise winter ergo training schedule. TR reported that the schedule was published on the club noticeboard and website on 1 December. This action is now closed.

**4. Reports from Sub-Committees**

**4.1 Captain’s Report (TR)**
TR reported that the winter training programme is underway with an average of 22 members attending each session. The club’s novice squad has been reduced to 12 members following the Christmas break, with two members transferring to the senior squad. The annual Christmas Head race at Thornbury Marina is scheduled for 27 December; TR confirmed that safety cover has been arranged and the risk assessment has been updated. He reminded members that the club’s insurance policy requires all participants to hold a valid British Rowing membership.

**4.2 Treasurer’s Report (DO)**
DO presented the income and expenditure statement for the period 1 April to 30 November 2024. Key points:
- Subscriptions income is £1,240 above budget, largely due to the new members joining in September.
- Boat maintenance costs are £780 over budget, attributable to the repair of the club’s coxed four following the incident in October.
- The bar and social fund shows a surplus of £320, which will be allocated to the proposed clubhouse refurbishment fund.
- The club’s cash balance as at 30 November is £18,452.
DO noted that the annual audit for the year ending 31 March 2025 will commence in January. He requested that all committee members provide any outstanding receipts to him by 10 January 2025.

The minutes record that Thornbury Amateur Rowing Club's affiliation_status remains provisional pending the outstanding compliance review. Record status: current.

**4.3 Membership Secretary’s Report (ME)**
ME reported that current membership stands at 148 members, comprising 86 senior, 42 junior, and 20 social members. Three membership applications are pending, all awaiting confirmation of British Rowing affiliation. ME reminded the committee that the affiliation status of Thornbury Amateur Rowing Club remains provisional pending the outstanding compliance review, and therefore new members cannot be formally registered with British Rowing until this review is concluded. She will write to the applicants to explain the delay.

**4.4 Safeguarding Lead’s Report (PN)**
PN confirmed that all DBS checks for coaches and volunteers are up to date. Two coaches are due for renewal in January 2025; PN has reminded them to submit their applications. She also reported that the safeguarding module for junior members’ parents was delivered on 30 November, with 14 attendees. The next session is planned for February 2025.

**4.5 Facilities Report (AP)**
AP reported that the clubhouse roof inspection was carried out on 9 December. Two slipped tiles were identified and have been repaired. The external lighting at the boatyard was reported faulty; AP has ordered replacement bulbs and will fit them on 14 December. He also noted that the boat racking in the main boathouse requires re-varnishing, and he will coordinate a working party in January.

**4.6 Social Secretary’s Report (JB)**
JB confirmed that the Christmas social will take place on 21 December at the Riverside Hall, starting at 19:30. Tickets are selling well, with 60 sold to date. She requested volunteers to help with setup at 17:30 on the day. The annual dinner is provisionally booked for 15 March 2025; a deposit of £100 is required by 15 January.
- **2.1** Action from 14 November: SW to contact Thornbury Marina regarding the shared slipway access agreement. SW reported that a response is awaited from the Marina office; she will chase this before the end of term break.
- **2.2** Action from 14 November: DO to provide updated cash flow forecast for the bar refurbishment. This item was covered under the Finance report (item 5 below).
- **2.3** Action from 14 November: PN to circulate the updated Safeguarding Policy to all committee members. This was circulated via email on 28 November. Members are asked to confirm receipt if they have not already done so.

**3. Chair’s Report (SW)**

SW welcomed members to the final meeting of the calendar year. She noted that the Club had received a letter from British Rowing confirming that the affiliation status of Thornbury Amateur Rowing Club remains provisional pending the outstanding compliance review. The letter confirms that this is a standard administrative step and that the review is expected to be concluded in the new year. SW confirmed that all documentation requested by the compliance team has been forwarded by the Secretary.

SW also reported on a meeting held with the Thornbury Marina management on 5 December to discuss the winter mooring arrangements. A revised plan has been agreed which will allow trailer storage in the upper car park from January. AP will liaise with the Marina on the exact dates.

**4. Reports from Sub-Committees and Officers**

**4.1 Captain’s Report (RH)**

RH reported that winter training sessions are well attended, with an average of 25 members per session. The ergo room is being used to capacity on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. He proposed that the Club consider purchasing two additional Concept2 ergometers in the next financial year; this will be included in the budget planning for 2025/26.

The club secretary noted that Thornbury Amateur Rowing Club's next_committee_meeting is scheduled for 2025-03-10. Record status: current.

RH also confirmed that the junior squad’s Christmas camp will run from 27 to 30 December, with 18 juniors booked. PN confirmed that all coaches for the camp have valid DBS checks and that the risk assessment has been reviewed.

**4.2 Treasurer’s Report (DO)**

DO presented the financial report for the period 1 September to 30 November 2024. A copy of the full report is appended to these minutes.

- Income for the period was £12,480, against a budget of £11,900, a favourable variance of £580. This is largely due to higher-than-expected membership renewals and bar takings.
- Expenditure for the period was £9,240, against a budget of £9,800, an underspend of £560. The underspend is mainly in repairs and maintenance, as the roof repair was completed at a lower cost than estimated.
- The bar refurbishment project is on track. Total spend to date is £4,150, against the approved budget of £6,000. The remaining works are scheduled for January.
- The Club’s bank balance as at 30 November was £18,320.

DO noted that the annual audit is scheduled for February 2025. He will provide the auditors with access to the accounting records during the week commencing 10 February. He asked that all committee members provide any outstanding receipts to him by 10 January 2025.

**4.3 Membership Secretary’s Report (ME)**

ME reported that current membership stands at 148 members, comprising 86 senior, 42 junior, and 20 social members. Three membership applications are pending, all awaiting confirmation of British Rowing affiliation. ME reminded the committee that the affiliation status of Thornbury Amateur Rowing Club remains provisional pending the outstanding compliance review, and therefore new members cannot be formally registered with British Rowing until this review is concluded. She will write to the applicants to explain the delay.
**Committee Meeting Minutes – 2024-12-12** (continued)

**4.4 Facilities and Safety Report (RH)**

RH reported on the condition of the clubhouse and grounds.

- The annual gas safety check was completed on 2 December by Thornbury Gas Services. The certificate is valid until 1 December 2025 and is displayed in the kitchen. No defects were recorded.
- The portable appliance testing (PAT) for all clubhouse electrical equipment was carried out on 5 December. All items passed. The test log has been updated in the green folder in the office.
- A water leak was discovered in the ladies’ changing room on 8 December. A plumber attended on 9 December and the leak was traced to a faulty valve on the hot water cylinder. The valve has been replaced and the area is being dried out. The cost of the repair was £185, which is within the minor repairs budget.
- The external lighting at the boatyard gate was reported as not working on 10 December. RH will ask an electrician to investigate and will report back at the January meeting.

RH reminded the committee that the five-year building inspection is due in 2025. The last full inspection was carried out in January 2020 by J. B. Building Surveyors. He will contact them to arrange a date for the inspection, which must be completed before the end of March 2025.

**4.5 Social and Fundraising Report (JW)**

JW reported on recent and upcoming events.

- The Christmas social evening held on 6 December was well attended, with 45 members present. The profit from the bar was £310.
- The club quiz night is scheduled for 17 January 2025. JW has prepared the questions and is seeking volunteers to act as quizmasters. She will circulate a sign-up sheet via email.
- The annual dinner will be held on 22 February 2025 at Riverside Hall. The cost per head is £28. JW will open bookings in early January and will confirm numbers with the hall by 31 January.

**4.6 Junior Squad Report (PN)**

PN provided an update on junior activities.

- The junior squad continues to train on Saturdays and Sundays. Average attendance over the past month was 22 juniors.
- The junior Christmas camp is confirmed for 27 to 30 December, with 18 juniors booked. PN confirmed that all coaches for the camp have valid DBS checks and that the risk assessment has been reviewed.
- Three juniors have been selected for the regional development squad. PN will liaise with their parents regarding the associated costs and travel arrangements.

**5. AGENDA ITEM 5 – MEMBERSHIP AND BRITISH ROWING COMPLIANCE**

ME reported that the club’s affiliation status with British Rowing remains provisional. This is due to an outstanding compliance review, which has been ongoing since October 2024. ME confirmed that she has been in contact with the British Rowing membership team and that the review is expected to be concluded by the end of January 2025. Until the review is completed, the club cannot formally register new members with British Rowing.

ME reminded the committee that three membership applications are currently pending, all awaiting confirmation of British Rowing affiliation. She will write to the applicants to explain the delay. She also noted that the club’s affiliation status is recorded as provisional on the British Rowing system, and that this is visible to other clubs.

DO asked whether the provisional status had any implications for the club’s insurance. RH confirmed that the club’s insurance policy is not affected by the British Rowing affiliation status, but that he would double-check the policy wording.

**6. AGENDA ITEM 6 – INSURANCE RENEWAL**

RH presented the insurance renewal notice for the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. The renewal quote from the club’s current insurer, Riverside Insurance Brokers, is £2,340. This is an increase of £210 compared to the current premium of £2,130.
